name: expo_simulators
description: Create, inspect and stop remote Android Emulator and iOS Simulator sessions.
long_description: Use an Expo personal or robot access token to create, inspect and stop remote simulator sessions without storing the Expo token on your Sprite. Saving or testing a token runs a read-only identity query and starts no simulator. The check does not verify project permissions or simulator availability. Device control uses the session-specific URL and credentials returned by Expo, outside this gateway. GraphQL, builds, account management and billing are not forwarded.

examples.title: Start an iOS session; replace PROJECT_ID (uses your Expo plan)
notes: Use an existing Expo Services project UUID for PROJECT_ID. Set platform to android for an Android Emulator. To install an app during startup, supply buildId, applicationArchiveUrl, or expoGo: true; choose at most one.

examples.title: Inspect a session; replace SESSION_ID
notes: Poll every five seconds until data.status is in-progress and data.remoteConfig is not null. Stop polling on stopped or errored. Treat remoteConfig as secret; it can contain controller and preview tokens. Connect your controller directly using these values.

examples.title: Stop a session; replace SESSION_ID
notes: Stop the session when finished, including after failures or polling timeouts. Closing a client does not stop the remote device.

messages.401: Expo access token is invalid; replace it in this connection
messages.403: Expo access token lacks permission for this project or operation; use a Developer-role token
messages.400: Expo rejected the request; check the project UUID, session options and simulator access for the account
messages.404: Expo project or session was not found
messages.429: Expo rate limit reached; retry later

presentation.tagline: Manage Expo simulator sessions without storing your Expo token on a Sprite.
presentation.setup: Create an access token at expo.dev/settings/access-tokens. For shared projects, use a robot user assigned the Developer role on the owning account. A personal access token also works. You need an existing Expo Services project and an account with Expo Simulators access.

notices.title: Billing
notices.body: Saving or testing a token only checks identity and starts no simulator. Sessions use your Expo plan’s resources and concurrency. Set maxDurationMinutes and stop each session when finished; closing your client does not stop it.

notices.title: Scope
notices.body: Only session creation, inspection and stopping are forwarded. GraphQL, builds, account management and billing are not forwarded. A successful token check does not verify project permissions or simulator availability.

notices.title: Device control
notices.body: The session response includes connection details for agent-device, Argent or Appium. Use those session credentials directly from your Sprite to control the device. These connections are outside this gateway; the Expo account token stays in Sprites. Treat controller and preview tokens as secrets, even for private previews.
